subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Greek Hades
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Greek Hades.

hook.text: The Greek underworld wasn't hell. Most souls drifted in Hades as shades—pale echoes of their former selves.

buildup.text: Five rivers bordered Hades: Styx for hate, Lethe for forgetting, Acheron for pain, and two more.

discovery.text: Elysium was reserved for heroes. Tartarus punished the wicked. Most souls got neither reward nor torment.

twist.text: The Greeks feared oblivion more than punishment. Being forgotten was worse than any afterlife torture.

climax.text: Hades was neither good nor evil—it was inevitable. Greek death was democratic: everyone faded equally.

punchline.text: Not punishment. Not reward. Just fading.

quiz.question: What did the river Lethe cause in Greek mythology?
